terms.gloss: The narrators' recurring epithet for Ostap Bender: a master schemer who lives by 'combinations'
terms.why_hard: Literal 'combinator' means nothing in English; the epithet recurs for the whole book and must be one fixed phrase with mock-grandeur

proposed.ja: 偉大なる策士

terms.gloss: The young con man, co-protagonist; also called 'Остап', 'Бендер', 'товарищ Бендер'
terms.why_hard: Spelling must be fixed once across en/zh/ja; Chinese and Japanese have several competing transcriptions

proposed.ja: オスタップ・ベンデル

terms.gloss: Former marshal of the nobility, now registry clerk; the narrators alternate 'Ипполит Матвеевич' and 'Воробьянинов'
terms.why_hard: Name+patronymic vs surname alternation is the narrators' tone device; must be preserved, not flattened to one form, and transliterated identically everywhere

proposed.zh: 伊波利特·马特维耶维奇·沃罗比亚尼诺夫
proposed.ja: イッポリート・マトヴェーエヴィチ・ヴォロビャニノフ

terms.gloss: Ostap's mock-corporate name for the two treasure hunters and their 'enterprise' (NEP-era concessions were state contracts with private/foreign capital)
terms.why_hard: Loses the joke if rendered as 'partners'; the NEP business register is the point, and it recurs with the mock titles below

proposed.zh: 特许经营者 / 特许经营公司
proposed.ja: 利権事業者たち / 利権事業

terms.term: директор-учредитель концессии; главный руководитель работ и технический директор
terms.gloss: Mock board titles: Vorobyaninov is founding director, Ostap chief of works and technical director
terms.why_hard: Must be rendered as deadpan corporate titles in a consistent set so later references ('технический директор') are recognisable

proposed.en: founding director of the concession; chief of works and technical director
proposed.zh: 特许公司创始董事；工程总负责人兼技术总监
proposed.ja: 利権事業の創立ディレクター；工事総責任者兼技術ディレクター

terms.term: предводитель дворянства / предводитель команчей / товарищ фельдмаршал / барон-изгнанник
terms.gloss: Ostap's chain of ironic epithets for Vorobyaninov; 'предводитель' means both 'marshal (of the nobility)' and 'chief (of the Comanches)'
terms.why_hard: The Comanche joke depends on the word 'предводитель' being the same in both; pick a marshal-of-nobility rendering that can be punned on

proposed.en: marshal of the nobility / chief of the Comanches / Comrade Field Marshal / the exiled baron
proposed.zh: 贵族首领 / 科曼奇人首领 / 陆军元帅同志 / 流亡男爵
proposed.ja: 貴族団長 / コマンチ族の首長 / 陸軍元帥同志 / 亡命男爵

terms.gloss: Pre-revolutionary yard-porter who sweeps, guards the gate and reports to the police; his basement lodge
terms.why_hard: 'Janitor' or 'caretaker' loses the servile, old-regime status Tikhon still lives in; the lodge is the concessionaires' base and recurs

proposed.zh: 看院人季洪 / 看院人的小屋
proposed.ja: 庭番のチーホン / 庭番小屋

terms.gloss: Housing department of the local soviet, which requisitioned furniture in 1919
terms.why_hard: Soviet acronym; must expand to a short readable phrase, never keep 'zhilotdel'

proposed.ja: 住宅課

terms.gloss: Old people's home No. 2 run by the social-security office (Стар- = старость, соцобес = социальное обеспечение); the text itself uses both spellings
terms.why_hard: Two acronyms for one place must map to one rendering; 'social security' in English sounds like a pension office, not a residence

proposed.en: Social Welfare Old Folks' Home No. 2
proposed.ja: 第二社会保障養老院

terms.gloss: Supply/housekeeping manager, a stock Soviet petty-official post; here also acting head of the home
terms.why_hard: Not 'manager' in the corporate sense; it is a low household-supplies post whose holder classically pilfers

proposed.ja: 総務主任（アリヘン）

terms.gloss: Chapter VIII title: a 'sky-blue', i.e. innocent, bashful petty thief who is ashamed of stealing
terms.why_hard: Modern Russian 'голубой' = gay; the 1928 sense is 'innocent, angelic'; a literal 'blue' or 'gay' reading ruins it

proposed.ja: 気弱なこそ泥

terms.gloss: Contraband moustache dye whose 'radical black' turns green; Vorobyaninov becomes 'the Titanic's victim'; chapter VII title 'Следы «Титаника»'
terms.why_hard: Brand name must stay 'Titanic' with a shipwreck echo; the epithet recurs and the title pun on 'traces/tracks' must survive

proposed.zh: “泰坦尼克”染发剂 / “泰坦尼克”的受害者
proposed.ja: 「タイタニック」/ タイタニックの犠牲者

terms.gloss: Odessa street proverbial as the source of all Soviet 'contraband', i.e. locally made fakes
terms.why_hard: The joke is that 'contraband' is home-made; a reader needs the counterfeit connotation carried in the sentence, not a footnote

proposed.zh: 敖德萨的小阿尔纳乌特街
proposed.ja: オデッサのマーラヤ・アルナウツカヤ通り

terms.gloss: Ostap's catchphrase 'the ice has started moving' = things are under way; a proverb in Russian
terms.why_hard: Must be one fixed phrase for the whole book so readers recognise the refrain; literal 'the ice has broken' is fine but must not vary

proposed.ja: 氷が動き出した！

terms.gloss: Ostap's catchphrase 'the session continues', echoing the Paris chamber president's words after Vaillant's 1893 bomb
terms.why_hard: Recurs as a refrain; needs a set formula, and a parliamentary register rather than 'meeting'

proposed.ja: 会議は続行する！

terms.gloss: Ostap's reproach: petty shopkeeper's mentality, versus living on a grand scale
terms.why_hard: 'Лавочник' carries Soviet contempt for the small trader; 'stinginess' alone loses the class sneer

proposed.en: shopkeeper's pettiness / Learn to live large!
proposed.zh: 小店主习气 / 学着大手大脚地活吧！
proposed.ja: 小商人根性 / 大きく生きることを学びなさい！

terms.gloss: Loose belted Tolstoy-style blouse, standard 1920s Soviet office wear (grey, velvet as a luxury)
terms.why_hard: In modern Russian 'толстовка' means a hoodie; a machine-minded translator will write 'sweatshirt'

proposed.ja: トルストイ・ブラウス

terms.gloss: Toile du Nord, cheapest grey cotton cloth issued to institutions; uniform of the old women and Alkhen
terms.why_hard: Not a colour and not a brand; a rendering must convey institutional cheapness on every repetition

proposed.ja: ねずみ色の安綿布（トワル・デュ・ノール）

terms.gloss: Primus kerosene pressure stove, the universal 1920s cooking appliance and fire hazard
terms.why_hard: Recurs throughout the book; 'stove' loses the kerosene and communal-kitchen connotation; keep as 'Primus'

proposed.ja: プリムス（石油コンロ）

terms.gloss: Soviet honorific 'Hero of Labour' (1927), used by Ostap ironically of the hungover yardman
terms.why_hard: Must be the official title form with capitals so the irony reads

proposed.ja: 労働英雄

terms.gloss: Orlov trotter, the prestige Russian breed raced separately from faster American-cross 'métis' trotters
terms.why_hard: The anecdote hinges on the two categories being kept apart; 'half-breed' or 'mongrel' misplaces the register

proposed.zh: 奥尔洛夫快步马 / 杂交马
proposed.ja: オルロフ・トロッター / 混血馬

terms.gloss: Aristide Briand, French premier and foreign minister famous for a heavy moustache
terms.why_hard: Reader must catch that he is the moustache benchmark; standard target-language spellings exist

proposed.ja: アリスティード・ブリアン

terms.gloss: Soviet acronyms in the dream sequence: Dnieper dam construction, the Butter Trust, the criminal investigation department
terms.why_hard: Book-wide policy needed: expand acronyms into short readable phrases, never transliterate them

proposed.en: the Dnieper dam works / the Butter Trust / the criminal police
proposed.zh: 第聂伯水电站工程 / 黄油托拉斯 / 刑侦局
proposed.ja: ドニエプル建設 / バター・トラスト / 刑事捜査部

terms.term: Марш вперед, труба зовет! / Парад — алле!
terms.gloss: Ostap's military and circus exit-cues: 'Forward march, the trumpet calls' and the ringmaster's 'Parade — allez!'
terms.why_hard: Recurring catchphrases; the circus register of 'алле' must not be mistaken for 'hello'

proposed.en: Forward march, the bugle calls! / Parade — allez!
proposed.zh: 前进，号声在召唤！/ 列队——出场！
proposed.ja: 前進、ラッパが呼んでいる！/ パレード、アレー！

terms.gloss: Opening of the 1920s salon romance 'Бубенцы', sung by the old women's choir
terms.why_hard: Verse must be rendered as singable rhymed lines and marked as a known song, not the authors' text

proposed.en: Hear the sleigh-bells ringing from afar
proposed.ja: 遠くから鈴の音が聞こえる

terms.gloss: Father Fyodor Vostrikov, the village priest who is the third treasure-hunter
terms.why_hard: Name spelling must be fixed once (Fyodor not Fedor/Feodor); the clerical title 'отец' must stay a title, not become 'father' as kinship

proposed.ja: フョードル神父

terms.gloss: an Orthodox priest's wife (the honorific used for her, not 'mother')
terms.why_hard: A literal 'mother' or 'Mummy' makes the reader think Fyodor is fleeing his mother; it is his wife

proposed.ja: 神父の妻

terms.gloss: NEP-era tax agent of the financial inspectorate, feared by private traders
terms.why_hard: Not a 'financial agent' or broker; it is a tax inspector, which is why the stallholder is buying him beer

proposed.ja: 税務査察官

terms.gloss: a NEP private trader running a market stall (палатка)
terms.why_hard: Not a tent-dweller or camper; a small private shopkeeper of the 1920s

proposed.ja: 露店商

terms.gloss: the railway right-of-way; used as a mock-solemn refrain ('Интересная штука — полоса отчуждения') for the whole world of stations and trains
terms.why_hard: The legal-surveying term is the joke; 'station' or 'railway' loses it, and the refrain recurs, so it must be rendered identically each time

proposed.ja: 鉄道用地

terms.gloss: railway porters, mock-heroically likened to Yermak, the Cossack conqueror of Siberia
terms.why_hard: The name means nothing to the target reader; the sense is 'burly bearded porters with the air of conquerors' and may need a half-line gloss inline

proposed.en: porters built like Yermak the conqueror of Siberia, in white aprons
proposed.zh: 身穿白围裙、活像征服西伯利亚的叶尔马克的搬运工
proposed.ja: 白い前掛けをした、シベリア征服者エルマークさながらの赤帽たち

terms.gloss: chapter IV title and recurring refrain; the 'muse of distant wanderings' that lures people across the country
terms.why_hard: It is a parody of Gumilyov's romantic phrase; keep it grand and slightly mocking, and identical in title and in text

proposed.ja: 遠い旅路のミューズ

terms.gloss: marshal of the nobility, the elected head of a district's gentry before 1917
terms.why_hard: Not 'leader' or 'chief of the nobles'; the fixed English term is 'marshal of the nobility', and the yard-keeper repeats it as a rank, not a job

proposed.ja: 貴族団長

terms.gloss: records clerk at the ZAGS, the civil registry office for births, marriages and deaths
terms.why_hard: The bathos of ex-marshal turned registry clerk depends on the office being humble and Soviet; 'ZAGS' alone means nothing to the reader

proposed.en: records clerk at the civil registry office
proposed.ja: 戸籍登録所の書記

terms.gloss: the former marshal of the nobility, Bender's partner; called Ippolit Matveyevich throughout
terms.why_hard: Name-and-patronymic address must be kept and transliterated the same way in every occurrence; do not shorten to a first name

proposed.zh: 伊波利特·马特维耶维奇·沃罗比亚尼诺夫
proposed.ja: イッポリート・マトヴェーエヴィチ・ヴォロビヤニノフ

terms.gloss: fictional provincial capital ('Old Town') where the chairs were confiscated; root of Старгубстрах, Старгуброзыск, Стардеткомиссия
terms.why_hard: Transliterate consistently and build the acronym-compounds on the same stem so the reader sees they are local offices

proposed.ja: スタルゴロド

terms.gloss: Soviet abbreviated agencies: provincial insurance, provincial criminal investigation, children's welfare commission, dairy cooperative centre
terms.why_hard: Opaque acronyms; render as short expanded names so the satire on alphabet-soup bureaucracy is visible but the meaning is not lost

proposed.en: Stargorod Provincial Insurance / Stargorod Provincial CID / Stargorod Children's Commission / Butter Centre
proposed.zh: 斯塔尔省保险局 / 斯塔尔省刑侦处 / 斯塔尔儿童委员会 / 乳品总社
proposed.ja: スタル県保険局 / スタル県刑事捜査部 / スタル児童委員会 / 乳製品センター

terms.gloss: the unnamed district town where the novel opens, in the Gogol/Chekhov 'town of N' tradition
terms.why_hard: 'N' is a literary convention, not an initial to be expanded; 'уездный' is a pre-revolutionary district, not a county

proposed.ja: 郡都N市

terms.gloss: 'non-Party', a standard box on every Soviet form (not a member of the Communist Party)
terms.why_hard: Not 'independent' or 'apolitical'; it is bureaucratic form-language recorded about a dead 59-year-old housewife

proposed.ja: 非党員

terms.gloss: Count Salias (E. A. Salias de Tournemire), prolific pre-1917 historical novelist, here remaindered at 5 kopecks
terms.why_hard: The joke is 'trashy old bestseller sold for nothing'; the name needs a two-word inline tag

proposed.ja: サリアス伯爵の小説

terms.gloss: the contraband hair dye that turns Vorobyaninov's moustache green; a running gag
terms.why_hard: Keep the brand in quotes and unchanged; later chapters refer back to it

proposed.ja: 「タイタニック」

terms.gloss: the protagonist, a charming con man; epithets 'великий комбинатор', 'сын турецко-подданного'
terms.why_hard: Spelling must be fixed once (Ostap Bender) and all epithets must map to him consistently

proposed.ja: オスタップ・ベンデル

terms.gloss: chapter V title and Bender's standing epithet: master schemer, operator
terms.why_hard: 'Combinator' is not English; needs a fixed epithet that sounds grand and ironic and is used every time

proposed.ja: 偉大なる策士

terms.gloss: 'a Turkish subject'; Bender's only stated biography (Odessa Jews sometimes took Ottoman citizenship to escape tsarist restrictions)
terms.why_hard: Keep the odd official phrase 'Turkish subject' verbatim; 'Turk' or 'Turkish citizen' flattens the hint and the recurring epithet

proposed.ja: トルコ臣民

terms.gloss: homeless street child of the post-Civil-War years (besprizornik), a fixture of 1920s towns
terms.why_hard: 'Homeless boy' loses the specific phenomenon; 'street urchin' is closer but needs one fixed rendering

proposed.ja: 浮浪児

terms.term: Может быть, тебе дать еще ключ от квартиры, где деньги лежат?
terms.gloss: Bender's retort to the beggar, now a Russian proverb for 'anything else you'd like?'
terms.why_hard: Must be rendered as a quotable line, plainly, since it is echoed later and is famous

proposed.en: Perhaps you'd like the key to the apartment where the money is, too?
proposed.zh: 也许还得把放钱的那套房子的钥匙也给你？
proposed.ja: ついでに、金の置いてある部屋の鍵も欲しいのか？

terms.gloss: Bender's joke for 'before the Revolution', using Marxist jargon as a calendar
terms.why_hard: Render 'historical materialism' literally so the joke of using doctrine as a date survives; the yard-keeper's 'old regime' is the plain counterpart

proposed.en: before historical materialism / under the old regime
proposed.zh: 历史唯物主义之前 / 旧制度时期
proposed.ja: 史的唯物論以前 / 旧体制の頃

terms.gloss: proverb: 'to some a mare is a bride', i.e. it depends who's asking
terms.why_hard: A literal rendering must still read as a folksy saying, not nonsense

proposed.en: To some a mare's a bride
proposed.ja: 牝馬でも嫁と思う者もいる

terms.gloss: Bender's recurring verdict on shoddy schemes: 'low grade, unclean work'
terms.why_hard: A catchphrase; fix one crisp rendering and repeat it verbatim wherever it recurs

proposed.ja: 下の下、仕事が汚い

terms.term: «Большевики пишут письмо Чемберлену» / «Запорожцы пишут письмо султану»
terms.gloss: Bender's planned parody of Repin's famous painting, keyed to the 1927 anti-Chamberlain propaganda campaign
terms.why_hard: Reader needs to know Repin's painting and that Chamberlain was the villain of 1927 Soviet posters; Kalinin and Chicherin are real Soviet leaders

proposed.en: 'The Bolsheviks Write a Letter to Chamberlain' / Repin's 'The Zaporozhian Cossacks Write a Letter to the Sultan'

proposed.zh: 萨马拉、奥廖尔、克列奥帕特拉、乌斯季尼娅、察里津、克列缅季、伊菲格尼亚、约克（原文按俄文字母逐个拼读）
proposed.ja: サマーラ、オリョール、クレオパトラ、ウスチニヤ、ツァリーツィン、クレメンチー、イフィゲニヤ、ヨーク（ロシア語綴りの一字ずつ）

terms.gloss: Tax inspector of the NEP era, the terror of private traders; the villain of the bedbug chastushka
terms.why_hard: Recurs as a stock NEP bogeyman across the novel; should be one fixed term, not 'financial inspector'

proposed.ja: 税務調査官

terms.gloss: Short rhymed comic folk ditties sung to balalaika; here 'Novgorod chastushki' on the radio
terms.why_hard: Not 'songs'; the verse must be rendered as doggerel with rhyme, and the genre name kept consistent

proposed.zh: 恰斯图什卡（民间俏皮小调）
proposed.ja: チャストゥーシカ（戯れ歌）

terms.gloss: Mattia Battistini, the Italian baritone idol of pre-war Russia; a 'black-earth Battistini' is a peasant singer from the steppe
terms.why_hard: Reader will not know Battistini; keep the name but signal 'celebrated baritone' once

proposed.zh: 黑土地上的巴蒂斯蒂尼（意大利名男中音）
proposed.ja: 黒土のバッティスティーニ

terms.gloss: Orphans of the 1921–22 Volga famine, a stock object of Soviet charity appeals
terms.why_hard: Literal 'children of the Volga region' loses that it is a famine-relief cliché Ostap is mocking

proposed.ja: ヴォルガ飢饉の孤児ですか？

terms.gloss: Soviet propaganda cliché used to explain any present ill
terms.why_hard: Must sound like a slogan the reader recognises as recycled jargon, not a fresh sentence

proposed.en: A grim legacy of the tsarist regime?
proposed.ja: 帝政の重い遺産ですか？

terms.gloss: The 'complex method', a 1920s Soviet progressive pedagogy fad; Ostap's sarcastic 'co-education of both sexes by the complex method'
terms.why_hard: Sounds like ordinary words but is a period educational term; needs a rendering that smells of jargon

proposed.ja: 総合教授法

terms.term: Александровский, ныне имени Пролетарских субботников, бульвар
terms.gloss: A boulevard renamed after the 'proletarian subbotniks' (unpaid Saturday volunteer labour); a joke about Soviet renaming
terms.why_hard: Subbotnik has no target equivalent; the renaming syntax must stay awkward on purpose

proposed.en: Alexander Boulevard, now Proletarian Saturday-Volunteers Boulevard
proposed.zh: 亚历山大林荫道（现名“无产阶级星期六义务劳动”林荫道）
proposed.ja: アレクサンドル大通り、現在は「プロレタリア土曜労働」記念大通り

terms.gloss: Short side-whiskers in the style of Nicholas I's reign, here on a woman's face
terms.why_hard: 'Nicholas' alone is ambiguous (I or II); the period look is 1830s–50s military

proposed.zh: 尼古拉一世时代式的短颊须
proposed.ja: ニコライ一世風の頬ひげ

terms.gloss: Vox humana, an organ (here harmonium) stop imitating the human voice; Ostap showing off
terms.why_hard: A Latin term garbled into Russian; keep it as Latin, not translated to 'human voice'

proposed.ja: ヴォクス・フマーナ

terms.gloss: 'Whatever God has sent': modest formula for pot-luck; the joke is that God sent Alkhen zubrovka and borscht with prime beef
terms.why_hard: The narrator reuses the formula literally in the next sentence; both must use the same words

proposed.zh: 上帝赏的什么就吃什么
proposed.ja: 神さまのお恵みのまま

terms.gloss: Bison-grass vodka; minced herring spread; small Black Sea sprats (the two kilos Pasha ate)
terms.why_hard: Period foods signal Odessa-Jewish and Ukrainian table; must be recognisable dishes, not generic 'vodka/fish'

proposed.zh: 野牛草伏特加 / 鲱鱼碎（福什马克）/ 黑海小鲱鱼
proposed.ja: ズブロッカ／ニシンのフォルシュマーク／黒海の小魚チュリカ

terms.gloss: The flea market / second-hand bazaar; Ostap's accusation that the extinguisher was bought there
terms.why_hard: Recurs in the novel as where stolen goods go; keep one colloquial word

proposed.ja: 蚤の市

terms.gloss: Institutional blankets woven with the word 'Feet' at one end so inmates lay them the right way round
terms.why_hard: Recurring gag; the word must be short, capitalised and identical each time

proposed.en: blankets woven with the word FEET
proposed.ja: 「足」と織り込まれた毛布

terms.gloss: The old women as 'wards' of the almshouse, a term normally used for schoolgirls; deliberately incongruous
terms.why_hard: Translating as 'residents' loses the mock-orphanage tone that sets up the 'sirоты' joke

proposed.ja: 院の「寄宿生」たち

conventions: Soviet acronyms (Старсобес, губпожар, Доризул): transliterate as a proper name and add a short parenthetical expansion at first occurrence in each chapter only; never expand inside dialogue
Dialogue dashes: en uses double quotation marks with one paragraph per speaker; zh uses “”; ja uses 「」; narrator interjections (сказал Остап) stay in the same paragraph as the speech

Ostap's mock-official speech (вы to Alkhen, bureaucratic phrasing) is rendered in ja with です・ます, and the narrator's voice in plain だ・である form; recurring refrains such as 'пожарной опасности не представляет' use one fixed wording book-wide

terms.gloss: Ostap's invented secret monarchist society; the name puns on the biblical 'swords into ploughshares' (меч/орало) and on орать 'to yell'
terms.why_hard: The chapter title and the society's name recur; a literal 'sword and plough' loses the archaic-biblical ring, and 'orala' must not be read as a verb

proposed.en: the Union of the Sword and the Ploughshare
proposed.ja: 剣と鋤の同盟

terms.term: гигант мысли, отец русской демократии, особа, приближенная к императору
terms.gloss: Ostap's mock-solemn triple title for Vorobyaninov, repeated verbatim throughout the book
terms.why_hard: It is a fixed formula and a running joke; each of the three parts must be rendered identically every time it recurs

proposed.en: giant of thought, father of Russian democracy, a person close to the Emperor
proposed.zh: 思想的巨人、俄国民主之父、皇帝身边的红人
proposed.ja: 思想の巨人、ロシア民主主義の父、皇帝側近の人物

terms.gloss: The narrator's standing epithet for Ostap Bender: a grand schemer/operator
terms.why_hard: Recurs across the whole book; 'combinator' is meaningless in English, and each language needs one fixed phrase with a wink of admiration

proposed.ja: 大策士

terms.gloss: Ostap's stock self-description ('son of a Turkish subject'), i.e. of an Odessa father who took Ottoman citizenship
terms.why_hard: Must not become 'a Turk'; the bureaucratic word 'subject' is the joke and the phrase recurs as Ostap's alias

proposed.ja: トルコ臣民の息子

terms.gloss: 'Bear up / stay firm' — Ostap's meaningless conspiratorial exhortation repeated to every guest
terms.why_hard: It must be one short identical phrase every time, since the comedy is in the mechanical repetition

proposed.ja: 気をしっかりお持ちなさい。

terms.term: Заграница нам поможет / Запад нам поможет
terms.gloss: 'Abroad will help us / the West will help us' — Ostap's slogan that became a Russian proverb
terms.why_hard: A proverbial line; render both variants with parallel wording and keep 'help us' as the fixed core

proposed.en: Abroad will help us / The West will help us
proposed.zh: 国外会帮助我们的 / 西方会帮助我们的
proposed.ja: 外国が助けてくれる / 西側が助けてくれる

terms.term: Полная тайна вкладов, то есть организации
terms.gloss: Ostap slips into the Soviet savings-bank advertising slogan 'complete secrecy of deposits' before correcting himself
terms.why_hard: The slip only works if the reader recognises a bank slogan; keep the word 'deposits' and let the self-correction stand

proposed.en: Complete secrecy of deposits — of the organisation, I mean.
proposed.zh: 存款绝对保密——我是说，组织绝对保密。
proposed.ja: 預金の秘密は厳守——いや、組織の秘密は厳守。

terms.gloss: 'Gentlemen of the jury' — Ostap's pre-revolutionary courtroom address, absurd in 1927 when juries no longer existed
terms.why_hard: Recurs as Ostap's oratorical tic; must keep the old-regime flavour ('gentlemen', not 'comrades')

proposed.ja: 陪審員の皆さん

terms.gloss: The homeless orphan street children of the 1920s, a mass social problem and a favourite target of Soviet charity appeals
terms.why_hard: 'Orphans' or 'poor children' misses that this was a specific, named category everyone was asked to donate for

proposed.ja: 浮浪児

terms.term: дети — цветы жизни / цветы улицы / цветы на асфальте
terms.gloss: Ostap riffs on the stock slogan 'children are the flowers of life'
terms.why_hard: The three variants must share the word 'flowers' so the parody of the slogan is visible

proposed.en: children are the flowers of life / flowers of the street / flowers on the asphalt
proposed.zh: 孩子是生活的花朵 / 街头的花朵 / 沥青路上的花朵
proposed.ja: 子供は人生の花 / 街の花 / アスファルトの花

terms.gloss: 'Proletarians of mental labour' — official euphemism for the intelligentsia
terms.why_hard: Should sound like Soviet officialese, not like a natural phrase

proposed.ja: 頭脳労働のプロレタリア

terms.gloss: Seasonal work away from home; here Ostap's sly euphemism for private trade under NEP
terms.why_hard: Too literal a rendering ('outside trades') obscures that the caviar-eaters are Nepmen

proposed.ja: 出稼ぎ稼業

terms.gloss: NEP-era private traders (Kislyarsky, Dyadyev); Ostap addresses them in the vocabulary of the class enemy
terms.why_hard: 'Merchants' is an old-regime word deliberately applied to Nepmen; keep the archaism

proposed.ja: 私的資本 / 商人衆

terms.gloss: The 'equalizing levy' (уравнительный сбор), a NEP turnover tax on private traders
terms.why_hard: Unexplained, 'the equalizer' is meaningless; needs a rendering that reads as a tax

proposed.ja: 均等税

terms.gloss: Pun on the tax-form category 'кустарь-одиночка с мотором' (self-employed artisan with a motor) — Polesov is a lone mechanic
terms.why_hard: The joke depends on a bureaucratic tax label; a short translator's note is probably unavoidable

proposed.en: a lone hussar with a motor
proposed.zh: 单干带发动机的骠骑兵
proposed.ja: モーター付き一人親方の軽騎兵

terms.gloss: Dyadyev's private firm, a parody of Soviet portmanteau names ('Quick-Pack')
terms.why_hard: Transliteration alone hides the joke; transliterate and gloss the compound once

proposed.ja: 「ブィストロウパク」（速包社）

terms.gloss: 'My business is sixteenth' — colloquial for 'none of my concern'
terms.why_hard: A literal number-rendering is gibberish in all three targets

proposed.ja: 俺の知ったことか

terms.gloss: Wedding-feast shout 'Bitter!' demanding that the newlyweds kiss
terms.why_hard: Must be explained once; thereafter keep a fixed form so readers recognise the custom

proposed.en: shouting 'Gorko!' (the wedding cry that makes the couple kiss)
proposed.zh: 喊“苦啊！”（婚宴上要新人接吻的起哄）
proposed.ja: 「ゴーリカ（苦い）！」と叫ぶ（新郎新婦に接吻をせがむ婚礼の掛け声）

terms.gloss: Opening line of Fet's poem, set as a much-sung parlour romance
terms.why_hard: Ostap is quoting; keep it as a quoted song title, not paraphrase

proposed.ja: 「夜明けに彼女を起こすな」

terms.gloss: Ostap's pet-name signature to the widow ('Your little Gopher')
terms.why_hard: Needs a cute animal name, not a zoological one, and the same one wherever the widow later repeats it

proposed.ja: きみのジリス

terms.gloss: The 'goods famine' — chronic NEP shortage of consumer goods
terms.why_hard: A period term; 'shortages' is too flat to carry Ostap's mock-thrifty joke about chintz

proposed.ja: 物資飢饉

terms.gloss: A vein bulging in the shape of izhitsa (Ѵ), the last letter of the pre-1918 alphabet
terms.why_hard: Needs both the shape and the archaic-letter joke; 'V-shaped' alone drops the humour

proposed.en: a vein in the shape of an izhitsa, the old alphabet's last letter Ѵ
proposed.zh: 一根青筋鼓成旧字母伊日察（Ѵ）的形状
proposed.ja: 旧字母イジツァ（Ѵ）の形に血管が浮き出た

terms.gloss: 'The meeting goes on' — Ostap's catchphrase, later a proverb
terms.why_hard: Recurs to the end of the book; fix one rendering now

proposed.ja: 会議は続く！

terms.gloss: Ostap's shifting nicknames for Vorobyaninov (field marshal, daddy, marshal of the nobility)
terms.why_hard: Each should be a stable word; 'предводитель' is an ex-rank, not a 'leader'

proposed.zh: 元帅 / 老爹 / 首席贵族
proposed.ja: 元帥 / 親父さん / 貴族団長

terms.term: улица Плеханова / бывшая Губернаторская / Карла Маркса
terms.gloss: Post-revolutionary street renamings that nobody, cabby or militiaman, can keep straight
terms.why_hard: Keep both old and new names literal so the 'formerly Governor's Street' joke survives

proposed.en: Plekhanov Street / the former Governor's Street / Karl Marx Street
proposed.zh: 普列汉诺夫街 / 原省长街 / 卡尔·马克思街
proposed.ja: プレハーノフ通り / 旧グベルナートル（知事）通り / カール・マルクス通り

terms.gloss: Soviet police officer (militsiya), as distinct from pre-revolutionary police
terms.why_hard: 'Policeman' erases the Soviet institution; keep one term book-wide

proposed.ja: 民警

terms.gloss: Horse-cab driver for hire, still the main urban transport in 1927
terms.why_hard: Not a 'taxi driver'; the horse is essential to the all-night wandering scene

proposed.ja: 辻馬車の御者

terms.gloss: Yard-keeper/janitor of an apartment house, also an informal local policeman
terms.why_hard: Not just 'janitor': the dvornik chasing Polesov is exercising quasi-police authority

proposed.ja: 庭番

terms.gloss: A loose belted shirt-blouse named after Tolstoy, typical 1920s office wear
terms.why_hard: Not a hoodie (modern sense) and not a sweater

proposed.ja: トルストイ・シャツ

terms.gloss: Narrator's ironic names for Ostap and Vorobyaninov, from Ostap's 'concession' for the chairs
terms.why_hard: Recurs throughout; 'concessionaires' must stay a fixed word and echo NEP foreign concessions

proposed.zh: 特许经营人 / 合伙人
proposed.ja: 利権屋たち / 相棒たち

terms.gloss: Suburb of the fictional Stargorod, seen from the train
terms.why_hard: Fictional place; transliterate consistently

proposed.ja: グシシチェ

terms.gloss: The Stargorod hotel and restaurant, pretentiously named
terms.why_hard: Keep the quotation-marked proper names, not 'the Sorbonne' as the university

proposed.en: the Sorbonne hotel / the Phoenix restaurant
proposed.ja: ホテル「ソルボンヌ」／レストラン「フェニックス」

terms.gloss: Two overgrown provincial youths, always named by childish diminutives
terms.why_hard: The diminutives are the characterisation; do not normalise to Nikolai/Vladimir

proposed.ja: ニケーシャとヴラージャ

conventions: Forms of address are a running joke and must stay distinct: гражданин = citizen/公民/市民, товарищ = comrade/同志/同志, господин/господа = Mr./gentlemen/先生/紳士諸君; Ostap's slips between them are kept, not smoothed.
Ostap's fixed formulas (giant of thought..., Bear up, The West will help us, gentlemen of the jury, The meeting goes on) are rendered by one identical phrase every occurrence in each language.

Dialogue dashes become target quotation marks (“ ” en, “” zh, 「」 ja); names are transliterated by one standard table per language (BGN/PCGN en, 新华社 table zh, katakana ja), patronymics kept, and Ostap addresses Vorobyaninov with вы rendered in Japanese as polite -ます form with mock deference.
